reviews.review_msg: Omar was not very helpful during my time in EDUC 400. His safety briefs, as our field school instructor, did not prevent students in my cohort from being robbed and hospitalized. We didn't go over anything that helped me as a TC, and I question why SFU works with someone who is not a certified K-12 teacher. EDUC 400 with Omar was unpleasant.

I will never forget Omar being aggressive with a classmate during our ending circle in one class in our field school. I did not like the lack of time and care in the activities we did in class, and the trip we paid thousands for didn't tie into becoming teachers at all, but more like tourist experiences. I do not recommend PDP ITEM or Omar.

My EDUC 400 class with Omar was not good. His safety briefings were only one slide and did not adequately prepare us to prevent the issues our cohort experienced. I found little of the course content helpful to my development as a TC. Omar is not a certified K-12 teacher, so I do not understand why he was teaching part of our EDUC 400 course.

We had lots of health and safety issues under Omar's watch. Omar seemed content to drop new activities on us randomly rather than keep an organized, field-based portion of our EDUC 400 course. I spent about 15k in tuition and fees over the 4 months and think that the Ollin activities were a waste of time and money. PDP ITEM with Omar was not good.

PDP ITEM with Omar was incredibly expensive, and I thought it would be worth it as it was marketed as a life-changing experience. Instead, we only did things that most tourists could do and had no set schedule or outline of activities. We often had to walk across town in the hot sun on a whim. I don't recommend Omar as a teacher, nor Ollin.

I did not have a good time in the PDP ITEM portion of the program Omar organized and led. Many of the lessons were performative, and when I checked after I got back home, many of the activities we were charged for cost much more than we should have. My group figures we paid 5-6x what the advertised cost for a Spanish lesson at Ollin would be.

Omar was a questionable choice to run our ITEM field school and EDUC 400. His activities were more aligned with activism and enriching himself and his Mexican partners than with making sure we developed as teachers. We only had 4 days of in-classroom time. I had several concerns around safety, Omar did not put much effort into the safety brief.

Omar is directly responsible for the SFU PDP ITEM program no longer running as of 2026. Due to his lack of preparedness, disorganization and inability to run a field school program in a responsible way, students were robbed and hospitalized when the program last ran. Omar did not take safety seriously and should not be in charge of field schools.
